attribution.note: Marcus writes about himself in the third person in the sign-off of his own newsletter. The sentence is his own words and he endorses them.

semantics.note: The claim is a firm present-tense statement that AI slop is serious and ubiquitous. The normalised version keeps that scope and adds nothing.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: 'ubiquitous' as widespread across many domains, and 'serious' as causing documented harm. Read literally, 'ubiquitous' would be hyperbole, so this reading is fair to Marcus. The result still turns on that interpretation, which he did not supply.

evidence.note: Ahrefs found AI content in 74% of 900k new web pages in April 2025, inside the target period. Caveats: it uses Ahrefs' own detector, most pages were mixed human and AI, and AI content is not always slop.
Engadget (April 2025) reports Deezer's figure that over 18% of daily music uploads are fully AI-generated. The figure is Deezer's own disclosure about its platform, but it shows a second domain.
A secondary summary (May 2025) of a database listing 116 court decisions in 12 countries that confirm AI-hallucinated content in legal filings. This shows documented harm in law, a third domain.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair plain reading, sources dated before the post show large volumes of AI content on the web and in music, plus documented legal harm across 12 countries. That meets the support condition of several domains plus harms. The packet lists no counterevidence. Caveats: the web and music figures come from the companies' own detectors, and there was no measurement for journalism, politics or education.
